payload.analysis: To maintain portfolio stability and predictable cash flows, I recommend a laddered maturity structure with bonds issued by high-credit-quality issuers. For a conservative portfolio, we can divide the investment into three maturity buckets: 2-3 years, 4-5 years, and 6-7 years. This structure allows us to manage risk and maintain liquidity while generating returns through coupon payments and capital appreciation. Specifically, I suggest allocating 30% to the 2-3 year bucket, 25% to the 4-5 year bucket, and 45% to the 6-7 year bucket. Within each bucket, we can invest in a mix of government bonds, investment-grade corporate bonds, and mortgage-backed securities from developed market issuers. This diversified portfolio will provide a stable income stream and help preserve capital. A key constraint we must address is the portfolio duration, which must remain below 10 years. To achieve this, we focus on short-to-intermediate term bonds. As a result, our recommended portfolio duration is approximately 7.2 years, which is below the maximum threshold. The proposed allocation to each maturity bucket is as follows: 30% to the 2-3 year bucket through high-grade investment (e.g., T-bills or short-term commercial paper) and 25% and 45% to the 4-5 year and 6-7 year, respectively, comprising high-grade corporate bonds (e.g., utilities, AA/Aaa).
